newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel mutual funds had negative returns in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Israel mutual funds had negative returns in 1996.

text.p: Most Israeli mutual funds posted negative returns in 1996, even though the stock and bond markets rallied in the last months of the year, Meitav Investments and Securities said.
"In spite of the improvement (in the capital markets) in the last months, it was still a difficult year for (the funds)," Meitav said in a statement released Wednesday.

Meitav's mutual fund index rose 6.5 percent for the year in nominal terms, but after discounting for last year's estimated inflation the index showed a decline of 3.6 percent. Only 40 percent of the 302 funds surveyed showed a positive return after inflation, Meitav said.

Share funds were responsible for the decline, averaging a 2.0 decline nominal decline for the year. In December, however, the share funds showed an 8.9 percent return, raising the general fund index 3.9 percent for the month.

"Progress in negotiations with the Palestinians on the subject of Hebron, the 0.5 percentage point reduction in Bank of Israel interest rates, the good odds that the 1997 budget would pass and the (low) level of share prices all joined together to create a positive atmosphere around the stock market," Meitav said about December.
For the year, bond funds did better than the share funds, showing an average nominal return of 14.4 percent.

The Tel Aviv Stock Exchange's general share index ended down 0.98 percent for 1996, or about 10.5 percent after inflation. The general bond index rose 13.2 percent, or about 2.3 percent after inflation.
